argument-null.title: ArgumentNullException
argument-null.short: null was passed to a parameter that does not allow it.
argument-null.summary: This exception is used when a method receives null for an argument it requires to be non-null.
argument-null.why: Continuing with a null argument would make the operation invalid, so the method fails early.
argument-null.tips: In your own methods, ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull provides a concise guard.

badNotes.7: null is passed to a parameter that does not allow it

goodNotes.2: Call the method only when the value is not null

argument-exception.title: ArgumentException
argument-exception.short: An argument value does not satisfy the method's requirements.
argument-exception.summary: This exception is used when the argument has the right type but its value itself is not acceptable.
argument-exception.why: The method is enforcing a constraint that cannot be expressed by the parameter type alone.
argument-exception.tips: Use ArgumentOutOfRangeException for range errors and ArgumentNullException for null when those communicate the cause more precisely.

badNotes.7: An empty string does not satisfy this method's requirement

goodNotes.1: Provide a value that satisfies the requirement

argument-out-of-range.title: ArgumentOutOfRangeException
argument-out-of-range.short: An argument is outside the allowed range.
argument-out-of-range.summary: This commonly occurs when an index, length, count, or similar numeric argument is outside the valid range.
argument-out-of-range.why: The requested range extends beyond the actual range of the collection.
argument-out-of-range.tips: Start by checking the argument name and actual value reported in the exception message.

badNotes.2: This requests 3 elements from a List containing only 2

goodNotes.2: Request a count within the actual range

invalid-operation.title: InvalidOperationException
invalid-operation.short: The operation is not valid for the object's current state.
invalid-operation.summary: The operation exists, but the current state of the object makes it invalid.
invalid-operation.why: An empty sequence has no element that First can return.
invalid-operation.tips: With LINQ, FirstOrDefault or SingleOrDefault may be appropriate depending on the intended behavior.

badNotes.2: First() is called on an empty sequence

goodNotes.2: Retrieve the value while accounting for an empty sequence

invalid-cast.title: InvalidCastException
invalid-cast.short: A value was cast to a type incompatible with its runtime type.
invalid-cast.summary: An explicit cast can compile successfully but still fail at runtime when the actual object type is incompatible.
invalid-cast.why: The object contains a string, and a string object cannot be treated directly as an int.
invalid-cast.tips: Use an is pattern to verify the runtime type before using it.

badNotes.2: The object contains a string, so it cannot be cast directly to int

goodNotes.2: Check the type and convert from text when needed

divide-by-zero.title: DivideByZeroException
divide-by-zero.short: An integer or decimal value was divided by zero.
divide-by-zero.summary: This occurs when the divisor is zero in integer or decimal division or remainder operations.
divide-by-zero.why: There is no integer result that represents division by zero.
divide-by-zero.tips: For double, division by zero does not produce this same exception and may result in Infinity or NaN.

badNotes.3: The divisor y is still zero

goodNotes.3: Verify that the divisor is nonzero before dividing

overflow-exception.title: OverflowException
overflow-exception.short: A numeric value exceeds the target type or checked operation range.
overflow-exception.summary: This can occur during numeric conversion or in a checked context when the result exceeds the representable range.
overflow-exception.why: The code is trying to store a result larger than the maximum value representable by int.
overflow-exception.tips: Unchecked integer arithmetic may wrap instead of throwing, so also watch for silent logic errors.

badNotes.2: This calculation exceeds the maximum int value

goodNotes.1: Use long when the required range is larger

io-exception.title: IOException
io-exception.short: A file or stream I/O operation failed.
io-exception.summary: IOException represents a broad range of input/output failures, such as a file already being in use or a device problem.
io-exception.why: Depending on file-sharing settings, the same file may not be openable a second time at the same moment.
io-exception.tips: Because IOException covers many causes, inspect both the exception message and InnerException when available.

badNotes.2: The same file is opened again while it is still in use

goodNotes.1: Use using to make the file lifetime explicit

directory-not-found.title: DirectoryNotFoundException
directory-not-found.short: A specified directory does not exist.
directory-not-found.summary: This can occur when part of a file path refers to a directory that does not exist.
directory-not-found.why: WriteAllText does not automatically create missing parent directories.
directory-not-found.tips: Directory.CreateDirectory is safe to call even when the directory already exists.

badNotes.1: This writes into a parent directory that does not exist

unauthorized-access.title: UnauthorizedAccessException
unauthorized-access.short: The program does not have permission to access a file or directory.
unauthorized-access.summary: This occurs when operating-system permissions, read-only state, or similar restrictions prevent the requested operation.
unauthorized-access.why: The user running the process may not have write permission for the target location.
unauthorized-access.tips: Before forcing a fix with administrator privileges, check whether the application is writing to an appropriate location.

badNotes.1: This location may not be writable by the current user

goodNotes.1: Choose a writable application data location

object-disposed.title: ObjectDisposedException
object-disposed.short: An object was used after it had been disposed.
object-disposed.summary: This occurs when code operates on an object such as a stream after that object has already been disposed.
object-disposed.why: Dispose has already released the resources owned by the object.
object-disposed.tips: Check whether an IDisposable object is being used outside the using scope that owns it.

goodNotes.1: Use using to manage the valid lifetime

not-supported.title: NotSupportedException
not-supported.short: The requested operation is not supported by this object.
not-supported.summary: An operation may exist on an interface or base type even when a particular implementation does not support it.
not-supported.why: A read-only collection can implement ICollection<T> while still rejecting Add operations.
not-supported.tips: When a type exposes capability properties such as CanRead, CanWrite, or IsReadOnly, check them before performing the operation.

badNotes.2: Add is called on a read-only collection

goodNotes.1: Use a mutable List when modification is required

operation-canceled.title: OperationCanceledException
operation-canceled.short: An operation was canceled through a CancellationToken.
operation-canceled.summary: This exception indicates that a cancellable operation received a request to stop.
operation-canceled.why: Operations that accept CancellationToken may report a cancellation request by throwing this exception.
operation-canceled.tips: Cancellation is not necessarily an error, so handle it separately from ordinary failures.

badNotes.3: Passing an already-canceled token reports cancellation

goodNotes.5: Handle cancellation separately from ordinary failure

task-canceled.title: TaskCanceledException
task-canceled.short: A Task was canceled before it completed.
task-canceled.summary: TaskCanceledException derives from OperationCanceledException and may appear when awaiting a canceled Task.
task-canceled.why: The Task entered the Canceled state instead of completing successfully.
task-canceled.tips: In many cases, catching OperationCanceledException is more useful than handling only TaskCanceledException.

badNotes.2: The Task is canceled before completion

timeout-exception.title: TimeoutException
timeout-exception.short: An operation did not finish within the allowed time.
timeout-exception.summary: This represents a communication or waiting operation exceeding its configured timeout.
timeout-exception.why: The operation took longer to finish than the duration supplied to WaitAsync.
timeout-exception.tips: Do not only increase the timeout; also investigate why the operation is slow and decide how retries should work.

badNotes.1: A timeout that is too short can produce TimeoutException

goodNotes.5: Define what should happen when a timeout occurs

uri-format.title: UriFormatException
uri-format.short: A string cannot be interpreted as a valid URI.
uri-format.summary: This occurs when constructing a Uri from text that has an invalid format.
uri-format.why: The string does not satisfy the structure required for the requested URI.
uri-format.tips: For external input, Uri.TryCreate validates the value without using an exception for control flow.

badNotes.1: An invalid URI string is passed directly to new Uri

goodNotes.1: Use TryCreate to verify that the URI is valid

regex-timeout-exception.title: RegexMatchTimeoutException and bounded matching time
regex-timeout-exception.short: Bound regex work and fix patterns that backtrack excessively.
regex-timeout-exception.summary: RegexMatchTimeoutException reports that matching exceeded a finite timeout. Nested ambiguous quantifiers can cause excessive backtracking on near-matching input.
regex-timeout-exception.why: The timeout bounds the runtime of the [[regex-basic|pattern search]] so one input cannot monopolize execution indefinitely.
regex-timeout-exception.tips: Reject the current input, inspect its size and the pattern, and simplify or use NonBacktracking where supported. Retrying the same work indefinitely does not solve the cause.

decoder-fallback.title: DecoderFallbackException and malformed byte sequences
decoder-fallback.short: Detect malformed input with a strict text decoder.
decoder-fallback.summary: Configure strict decoding to reject malformed bytes instead of silently replacing them with fallback characters.
decoder-fallback.why: Silent replacement can hide damaged or incorrectly encoded input when exact text recovery matters.
decoder-fallback.tips: Choose the Encoding and the rejection-versus-replacement policy explicitly when performing [[encoding-text-bytes|text/byte conversion]].

end-of-stream.title: EndOfStreamException and truncated data
end-of-stream.short: Handle a stream ending before a complete value can be read.
end-of-stream.summary: EndOfStreamException can occur when a typed reader reaches the end before enough bytes are available to reconstruct the requested value.
end-of-stream.why: A partially available fixed-size record cannot safely be treated as a complete value.
end-of-stream.tips: For raw Stream.Read calls, also account for [[stream-short-reads|short reads]] and verify a complete record before decoding it.

http-request-exception.title: HttpRequestException and HTTP request failures
http-request-exception.short: Separate transport failure from an HTTP status response.
http-request-exception.summary: HttpRequestException represents transport failures and can also represent HTTP responses explicitly converted into exceptions.
http-request-exception.why: Receiving a 404 response is operationally different from failing to receive an HTTP response at all.
http-request-exception.tips: Classify [[operation-canceled|cancellation]] and deadlines separately from transport failure so the caller retains the reason the operation stopped.

aggregate-exception.title: AggregateException and observing multiple failures
aggregate-exception.short: Inspect failures from several tasks combined into one operation.
aggregate-exception.summary: Inspect all exceptions stored on a faulted combined Task and distinguish them from the exception rethrown directly by await.
aggregate-exception.why: Several independent operations may fail, so observing only the first surfaced failure can omit useful diagnostic information.
aggregate-exception.tips: Keep the Task returned by [[task-whenall|Task.WhenAll]] so Exception.InnerExceptions remains available after the await fails.
